How do med spas get more clients from Google and AI search?

Short answer

Phoenix has a lot of med spas, so many people choose from the few that Google Maps and AI tools name first. Spas that get named tend to have a complete Google profile, every treatment listed by name, steady recent reviews, real photos, and clear answers about who performs treatments and how to book. The SocialDM's LocalLift program shows a med spa where it is named today and which gaps to close first.

The SocialDM · Nov 11, 2026
The problem

What helps a med spa get named

01Every treatment by name. Neurotoxin (such as Botox®), filler, laser hair removal and facials each listed on Google and each with its own page, not one "services" line.
02Who does the work. Names and credentials of the people performing treatments.
03Real photos. The actual rooms and team, not stock images.
04Plain answers. Price ranges or starting prices, consults, booking and parking.
05Fresh reviews. A steady flow, not a burst from two years ago.
Keep claims honestSkip promises of guaranteed results. They cause trouble with advertising rules and with clients. Show real results only with client consent, and never promise a before and after.
FAQ

Questions we hear

Do Google posts help a med spa rank?

Google says local results are mainly based on relevance, distance and how well known a business is. Posts keep your profile current and give people a reason to choose you, alongside reviews and complete info.

We already run ads. Do we still need this?

Ads stop when the budget does. Being named in Maps and AI answers can keep working between campaigns.
